d: Estimates the due date by adding 7 days to the first day of the last menstrual period and subtracting 3 months. It assumes a regular 28-day cycle, so irregular cycles need ultrasound dating.

Shorthand for obstetric history. G is gravidity, every pregnancy including the current one. P is parity, births at 20 weeks or later. The TPAL digits count term births, preterm births, abortions and living children.
Fluid under the skin at the back of the fetal neck, measured by ultrasound at 10 to 13 weeks. A thick measurement suggests aneuploidy, especially trisomy 21, and sometimes a heart defect.

A maternal blood test, possible from 10 weeks, that measures placental DNA fragments to screen for trisomies 21, 18 and 13. It is the most sensitive aneuploidy screen but is not diagnostic, so a positive result is confirmed.
An enzyme that leaks from exposed fetal neural tissue into amniotic fluid. A positive amniotic fluid result with a raised amniotic AFP confirms an open neural tube defect.
Weeks 3 to 8 after fertilization, when the organs form. Teratogens in this period cause major structural malformations, while exposure in the first 2 weeks is all or none.
Severe shortening or absence of the long limb bones, so the hands and feet attach close to the trunk like flippers. It is the signature defect of thalidomide exposure in weeks 4 to 8.

Injury from prenatal alcohol, with growth restriction, microcephaly, short palpebral fissures, a smooth philtrum, a thin upper lip and intellectual disability. It is the leading preventable cause of intellectual disability.
An ultrasound sign of open spina bifida with a Chiari II malformation: the cerebellum is pulled down and wrapped around the brainstem. The lemon sign, scalloped frontal bones, accompanies it.
